about: Labels for requests.json, written by reading the notes; one entry per request.

cases.why: The freezer note names the call list on the door, Marco first and Elena second; the no calls before 10:00 habit does not apply to an alarm.
The onboarding checklist lists the week one tasks: card, EHS courses, LabDrive and ELN accounts, tour, buddy and handbook.
No note names a primer supplier; the supplier note gives the framework supplier for general reagents and the off-framework check.
Booking is in FacilityHub after induction with a 4-hour daytime cap; the red laser on the spinning disk is still down next week.
No note says where another autoclave is; only the rule that BSL-2 solid waste must still be autoclaved bears on the message.
No note covers ethidium bromide; the chemical waste route helps, and the bleach then sink rule for virus waste must not be applied.
Cooking question, nothing to do with the lab.
The granule paper agreement (shared first, the draft writer named first) and the general first author rule answer it.
1,800 EUR needs Elena's tick but no quotes; the grant must fit the purchase and RRC takes no new equipment.
The Kestrel format note gives the page cap and Elena's running order of findings, then risks and changes; the renewal is a different document.
No note holds the presenter rota; the format notes say next week is a Wednesday 10:00 data talk.
The format gives one data talk per Wednesday and journal club on the last Wednesday of the month; the roster gives the nine names.
B214 access comes only after BSL-2 training and the handbook, with Tomasz keeping the BSL-2 register.
General coding exercise, nothing to do with the lab.
Raw files go to the VargaLab-Raw research share within a week and never only on a laptop; LabDrive is for protocols.
Raw data is kept 10 years after the last paper that uses it.
No miniprep steps are in the notes; the protocols note says where approved VL-P versions live and that drafts need Elena's signature.
Marco orders from the Orders sheet on Mondays and Thursdays; the usual quantity is not recorded; FBS is cell work, so it goes on KF-2024-031.
Registration BR-2024-063 covers third-generation lentiviral vectors, but only in B214 by registered users.
No note covers human samples or their approvals; the BSL-2 registration and fish licence are other paperwork, and the core manager Priya is someone else.
General knowledge question, nothing to do with the lab.
The hood note shows the lab has two hoods in B210 that PFA, phenol and chloroform work depends on; the yearly biosafety inspection is a different one.
The October statement gives KF-2024-031 at 61,400 EUR uncommitted with 12,000 EUR set aside for imaging, and only RRC has a consumables split.
No note covers controlled substances; Marco's ordering role does not answer who may sign for them.
The onboarding checklist covers card, desk, EHS courses and buddy; no desk location or session dates are recorded, and the fish licence course is not safety training.
New starters never work out of hours, others use the lone worker app, and nobody does hazardous or BSL-2 work out of hours.
Car question, nothing to do with the lab.
The storage note points to the existing Kestrel data management plan and the lab's storage and 10-year retention rules.
Expired chemicals go out as labelled chemical waste with the pickup form by Monday 12:00; Marco usually files it.
A machine over 5,000 EUR needs three quotes and Elena's approval, RRC takes no new equipment, and the cost must fit a grant's aims and dates.
Liquid nitrogen is not in the notes; Marco looks after stock and ordering, so he is the one to ask.
Maths question, nothing to do with the lab.
Lab meeting is Wednesday 10:00, not Tuesday, with one talk, short updates and admin at the end.
No leaver checklist exists; leavers hand raw data folders to Jonas before their account closes.
The convention says generating data shown in the paper earns co-authorship, recorded in the paper's authorship log.
Phenol and chloroform belong only in the hood and Samuel is safety rep and first aider; the bleach spill procedure is for biological spills.
Personal gift question, nothing to do with the lab.
Onboarding with a postdoc buddy, weekly data talks and journal club, and mentors as first contact are what the lab actually does.
